title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 65-68 of the 1986 'Analysis situs' draft): 𝔉 is a set of 'figures' (subsets of an ambient space) and 𝔐 ⊂ 𝔉 a distinguished subset. Both carry the symmetric relation 'disjoint' (an orthogonality, later abstracted as a compatibility relation R on an ordered set). For a family Φ, p.66 defines cosupp(Φ) = {F | F disjoint from every H ∈ Φ} and supp(Φ) = cosupp(cosupp(Φ)). This is the Galois connection (polarity) of the orthogonality relation.

This page states its standard consequences.
(1) Every subset of 𝔉 (resp. 𝔐) lies in a smallest saturated subset, its 'support' = the double cosupport.
(2) The saturated subsets are exactly the cosupports of arbitrary subsets.
(3) cosupp is an inclusion-reversing involutive bijection of the set of saturated parts onto itself. Restriction to 𝔐 (𝔐₀ = 𝔉₀ ∩ 𝔐) and 𝔉₀ = {F | F ⊂ 𝔐₀} identify the saturated parts of 𝔉 with those of 𝔐.

The resulting set Σ of 'supports virtuels' has two realisations, σ ↦ M_σ ⊂ M and σ ↦ F_σ ⊂ F. Σ is a complete lattice: inf is intersection, sup is the saturation of the union. Cosupport is an order-reversing involution (an orthocomplementation) on Σ.

On p.68 Grothendieck guesses that Σ is a complete Boolean algebra ('ultra-stonienne'), i.e. the clopen algebra of an extremally disconnected Stone space. He shows that Σ depends only on (M, ≤, R). In the margin he records distributivity in the set-theoretic examples.

Purpose: to attach to a tame-topology 'analysis situs' structure an intrinsic algebra of virtual supports. These are supports of families of figures, not necessarily realised by an actual subset.
errors: The lattice of Galois-closed sets of an arbitrary orthogonality (disjointness) relation is only a complete ortholattice, not necessarily distributive. Any symmetric irreflexive relation can be realised as set-disjointness, by assigning one point to each non-orthogonal pair. For example, four figures a, a', b, b' with only a⊥a' and b⊥b' give the non-distributive lattice MO2. So the guess on p.68 that Σ is Boolean needs an extra hypothesis: separativity, e.g. that two non-disjoint figures contain a common nonempty figure, as for open sets or a poset with compatibility = common lower bound. Under that hypothesis Σ is the regular-open (Boolean completion) algebra and is indeed complete Boolean. Grothendieck's own hedging ('présume', distributivity checked only in the 'ensembliste' case) suggests he was aware the guess was unproved.
Wording: the bijection is of the set of saturated parts onto itself (an involution), not 'of one onto the other'. The text corrects this implicitly by calling it an anti-automorphism of ordered sets.

ideas.what: Double-orthogonal closure (support = cosupp∘cosupp) of families of figures under the disjointness relation; saturated parts = Galois-closed sets
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity of an orthogonality relation (Birkhoff polarity; orthogonality spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1940); Ore; Foulis–Randall / MacLaren for orthogonality spaces

ideas.what: Σ = 'supports virtuels' as a complete lattice with an order-reversing involution, conjecturally a complete Boolean algebra whose Stone space is extremally disconnected ('ultra-stonien')
ideas.modern_name: Regular-open algebra / Boolean completion of a separative poset; Gleason cover (Stonean space); double-negation sublocale
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1937), Gleason (1958), Dixmier (Stonean spaces), Cohen–Scott–Solovay (Boolean completion in forcing), Lawvere–Tierney (¬¬-sheaves)

ideas.what: Σ depends only on the ordered set M together with a compatibility relation R (complement defined via R), not on the realisation of figures as subsets
ideas.modern_name: Boolean completion RO(P) of a forcing poset; ¬¬-sheaves on a poset

missed.claim: In his tame-topology 'analysis situs', Grothendieck independently arrives at the forcing/Gleason construction: a complete Boolean algebra of 'virtual supports' attached to a poset with a compatibility relation, conjecturally extremally disconnected. This links o-minimal/tame-topology figure structures to Boolean completions, Gleason covers and ¬¬-sheaves. The link is standard in its parts, but not made in the tame-topology literature to my knowledge.
missed.quote: On désignera par Σ l'ens. des supports virtuels, ou parties saturées
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest: it suggests attaching to an o-minimal or definable-set structure its regular-open/¬¬ Boolean algebra as an invariant of 'virtual supports'. The construction itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine (though unpublished) development of a Galois-closure/orthocomplementation. Its only interest is that Grothendieck rediscovers the regular-open/Boolean-completion picture inside his 1986 analysis situs, with a Boolean conjecture that is false without a separativity hypothesis.
transcription_corrections: 'bijection de l'une des parties saturées sur l'autre' is more likely 'bijection de l'ens. des parties saturées sur elles-mêmes' (an involution).
'On désignera par Σ l'un des supports virtuels' should read 'l'ens. des supports virtuels'.
'On identifiera [?] Σ et [?] en deux réalisations' is probably 'On identifie Σ à ses deux réalisations (comme partie de 𝔓(M), ou de 𝔓(F))'.
'qui sera notée [?] support (resp. cosupport)' should read 'qui sera notée supp (resp. cosupp)', with 'et s'appelle aussi son support'.
Struck first line: 'On a une notion de ...'.
